newsitem.title: USA: Boeing CEO sees stable order environment.
newsitem.headline: Boeing CEO sees stable order environment.

text.p: Boeing Co Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Phil Condit said Monday he thought the current airplane order rate could be sustained for the next several years.
Speaking to reporters after the company's annual meeting, he and other Boeing executives said they did not see the "buying frenzy" of the late 1980s and early 1990s.

In response to a shareholder question at the meeting, Condit said declining profit margins projected for the rest of 1997 were being caused by a mix shift to the manufacturer's newer 777 and next generation 737 models. But he said he was "very optimistic" about the overall prospects for both the company's commercial airplane business and its defense and space operations.
"I'm very optimistic about the upturn in our commercial airplane business as well as our prospects in defense and space," Condit said. "We're excited about the future of this company."
Condit also said he was confident Boeing's planned merger with McDonnell Douglas Corp would go through despite questions raised by European Union authorities.
He said Boeing tentatively had set a special shareholders meeting for July 25 to approve the merger.
Condit told reporters after the meeting that Boeing's airplane production rate, scheduled to go to a record 40 units a month by the end of this year, could go even higher in 1998.
"There is a possibility we could go higher," he said, adding that the company had encountered no "systemic" issues so far in rapidly increasing production rates.
